prompt:
Flat sumi-e ink wash painting on aged warm paper. Hand-painted, not rendered. A single isolated subject on plain paper, centred, whole subject in frame. Dark tapering brush outline, flat even ink-wash fill, uniform ambient tone with no visible light source, no cast shadow, no sheen. Monochromatic warm grey from pale paper to near-black ink. Brush character at every edge.

Subject: one far-away mountain ridge seen through haze, as a pale silhouette. A jagged sawtooth range of five or six uneven pointed peaks of different heights, the tallest one right of centre. It is wide and low, about four times wider than it is tall. Painted in exactly two pale values and nothing darker: a flat pale grey wash for the body of the ridge, and one soft, slightly darker brush stroke running along the top of the ridge line. For this distant subject there is no hard outline: the ridge line is that one soft stroke. The lower part of the ridge thins out and fades softly into bare paper, with no bottom edge. It is far away: everything stays pale, the darkest tone is a light-to-middle grey. The reference image is a piece of the original painting: take the brush handling, the ink values and the paper from the far ridge on the horizon in it, but paint only the subject described here.

Plain empty aged-paper background and nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no figure, no gate, no path, no sun, no moon, no birds, no text, no seal, no border, no frame. The paper is one flat even pale tone from edge to edge, with no vignette and no dark corners. Whole subject in frame with a clear margin of bare paper all round. Strictly monochrome warm grey: no blue, no green, no brown tint.
